summary: 1934 NC Forest Service steel tower on a Henderson County summit, staffed by Clyde Curtis from 1957 until the 1990s; trail reopened 2025 from one side only after Helene.

facts.design: 47-foot Aermotor tower with a 7 by 7 ft metal cab
facts.status_note: Listed as standing; the register and Conserving Carolina describe the tower in present or past tense, but no 2026 source confirms its condition.

access.note: The summit trail reopened in July 2025 only from the Edneyville side, after Hurricane Helene closures. Access to the tower itself is not confirmed.

visit.trail_note: Trail reached from the Edneyville side. Routes through Gerton, including Highway 74-A and the lower Bearwallow Mountain Road, were still closed at the July 2025 reopening.

events.note: NC Forest Service constructed the 47-foot steel tower; a state report of the 1932-34 biennium names it as the only tower bought with state budget money.
Clyde Curtis began staffing the tower; he later lived on the summit year-round.
Curtis lived on the summit until 1992; the tower was decommissioned a few years later.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, April 2, 2008.
Register projected restoration for 2011 to 2012. No source read confirms the work was done.
Summit trail closed after Hurricane Helene damage in September 2024.
Trail reopened in July 2025, from the Edneyville side only.

notes_for_editor: Built year 1934 is supported by the register and a state report quoted on a lookout-history site. Search snippets (not opened) gave a 1933 date (SummitPost) and a CCC-built 1937 date (Conserving Carolina); the Conserving Carolina page I read has no construction date, so neither is used. Search snippets also mention a padlocked chain-link fence and a 2016 blog on restoration plans; not verified, not used. The tower's current condition is the main gap: contact NC Division of Forest Resources District 9 or Conserving Carolina before publishing. The brief's 1934 build, 14.3 m height and 2008 registration match the sources and were kept.
